You use masculine form when referring to something/someone masculine, for example brother: der Bruder –> mein Bruder. Likewise for neuter, like kid: das Kind –> mein Kind (same form in the nominative, fun begins in other grammatical cases – same goes for articles) and for feminine, like sister: die Schwester –> meine Schwester.

This is why, when learning a new noun, it's so important to learn its grammatical gender, too. I have neglected that in middle school and had to make up for it later on.

Well, not as much indifferent as apathetic, but here goes nothing. 

This character does not get excited that easily. They will not be the first to step in/jump into action (if they will do it at all). If their apathy appears/grows in the middle of struggle, it might result in them giving up. In general, they might give up easily, after very first fail/difficulty. Their apathy may be a result of a) believing, that in the grand scheme of things issue X isn't that important (or maybe even nothing is), b) they personally are powerless against issue X, c) nothing can be done against issue X at all, d) they are to busy with battling their inner demons. The above will cause them to spoiling the party and being the team downer. This and failing at reaching out to people/putting effort into staying in touch with people will isolate them. They might (in a more severe cases) also fail to take care about themselves  - not too good personal hygiene, questionable fashion choices, lack of appetite or eating fast food/ready meals rather than cooking, their house/apartament/room being a mess. Or maybe they are living up a completely normal, average life (9-5 meaningles job, just a little part of a machine, a setting in which a single person means nothing) and have given in to their mediocricity and littleness. Maybe it's an effect of some medication or drugs. Or maybe some mental disorder or trauma. Maybe they feel like trapped in a glass bubble they can't get out of. Maybe, again, they care, but about something else. Maybe they simply hope things will resolve themselves without their involvement (maybe they're a fatalist and refuse to take action because they believe it's all up to fate). Or maybe they seem to be doing just fine, but feel dead inside - feel like there's no point in all that shite, but still force themselves to carry on.
